input.quote: Customer will use the Services only for its own internal business purposes to service its banking customers and clients and will not sell or otherwise provide, directly or indirectly, any of the Services or any portion thereof to any third party
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no non-compete or field-of-use covenant binding Customer: searches for "compete", "competing", "shall not develop/market", territory and exclusivity language return nothing that restricts the businesses Customer may operate or the products it may buy or build. The closest provisions are conventional scope-of-use limits rather than restrictive covenants: § 21.7(B) (p0273) confines Customer's use of the Services to its own internal business purposes and bars reselling the Services to third parties, and § 23.5 (p0313) limits any escrowed source code to Customer's internal processing and to the then-existing applications/functionalities. Neither prevents Customer from operating any line of business, developing its own systems, or acquiring or buying products elsewhere. § 10.3(A) (p0183) requires Customer to obtain Monthly Base Fee Services from M&I during the Term; that is a sourcing/minimum-purchase term reviewed under EXCLUSIVITY/MINCOMMIT and is not flagged twice here. The rule therefore sits at the preferred position and no redline is proposed.
